newsitem.title: INDIA: India Canara Bank posts 41 pct fall in net profit.
newsitem.headline: India Canara Bank posts 41 pct fall in net profit.

text.p: India's state-run Canara Bank posted a net profit of 1.47 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, 1997, down from 2.52 billion in the previous year, the Business Line newspaper reported at the weekend.
Canara Bank is one of India's leading banks.
The steep fall in profit was on account of provisions for income tax, depreciation and non-performing assets, it said, quoting a bank statement.
"Though the bank has not given a break-up of its provisions, the aggregate provisions towards the above amounted to 5.07 billion rupees for 1996/97 (April-March)," the paper said.
The bank reduced its dividend payment to 239 million rupees against 505 million a year ago, it said.
"The equity base of the bank remained unchanged at 4.84 billion with the bank having deferred its public issue."
The capital adequacy ratio too slipped to 10-17 percent from 10.38 percent, the paper said.

"The bank however managed to maintain its growth in deposits which went up by over 52 billion rupees to touch 314.45 billion rupees... The deposit growth at 20 percent was better than last year's 16.77 percent," it said.
The bank's lending improved by 13.17 billion rupees during the year to 144.13 billion rupees. Priority sector lending accounted for 49.5 percent, the bank said.
